summary: FDA granted De Novo DEN250005 on Jan 16 2026 for Sana Device as a prescription audio-visual stimulator for adjunctive temporary relief of neuropathic pain in adults.

BMC Neurology 2026 sham-controlled RCT in 75 chronic neuropathic pain participants found active device superiority over sham at Week 14 on NPSI total; no serious/unanticipated AEs; Sana funded study and company staff coauthored.
PTSD pilot RCT in veterans reported improvements in PTSD, anxiety, depression, and quality of life with Sana plus treatment as usual; Sana states device is not cleared for PTSD.
Founder origin story describes severe nerve-damage pain after accident, prototype relief, and decades of pain-free life.
Company explains AVS as coordinated light/sound pulses intended to entrain neural activity and resemble meditative-state effects.
Older FAQ/news language describes Sana as general wellness and not FDA-approved for a specific medical condition, creating stale-public-copy tension after 2026 De Novo.
Privacy policy lists contact/profile data, diagnostic self-reports, journal entries, demographics, geolocation, transactions, usage, device use, heart-rate data, and Firebase analytics.
Return policy requires RMA and device inspection; subscription continues until device returned and inspected; shipping/handling/taxes not refundable.
